purpose: This is a balance scale for solving equations. Each move you make happens on both pans, so the beam stays level and you see why it is allowed. You are trying to get x alone on one side.

stops.title: The scale
stops.text: The bag marked x holds a hidden number of blocks. The two pans are the two sides of the equation, shown at the top. A green = means the beam is level. On a wide screen, the Written work box lists every move and why it is allowed.
stops.try: Do one move and watch the pans, the equation and the Written work together.

stops.title: Balance or Formulas
stops.text: Balance uses the scale with bags and blocks. Formulas drops the scale and asks you to solve a formula like d = rt for one letter, using the same moves on both sides.
stops.try: Press Formulas, then come back with Balance.

stops.title: Pick a problem
stops.text: The menu is sorted from one-step equations up to harder ones, with x on both sides or parentheses. Choosing one starts it fresh.
stops.try: Pick a Two steps problem and plan the order before you press anything.

stops.title: Choose the amount
stops.text: Set what you will add, subtract, multiply or divide by. The plus and minus buttons change the number. The x button makes the amount a number of bags of x, for equations with x on both sides.
stops.try: Set the amount to 4 and read the four operation buttons.

stops.title: Do it to both sides
stops.text: Add, Subtract, Multiply and Divide use your amount on both pans at once. With an x amount only add and subtract work, because dividing by x could mean dividing by 0. Distribute and Swap sides appear when they apply.
stops.try: Press Subtract with the amount that clears the number next to x.

stops.title: What if only one side?
stops.text: This does the move on the left pan only, so the beam tips and the equation is false. Press it again (it becomes Put it back) to level the beam. It only shows in Balance mode.
stops.try: Try it once, then put it back.

stops.title: Hint, Undo, Reset
stops.text: Hint glows the next good operation and fills in the amount for you. Undo takes back your last move. Reset restarts the problem. When x is alone, a button appears to check the answer with numbers.
stops.try: Make a wrong move on purpose, then press Undo.

stops.title: Next and Back
stops.text: The four steps load a one-step problem, a two-step problem, one with parentheses, then a formula in Formulas mode. They only choose the problem, so you do the moves.
stops.try: Press Next, then try to solve it before reading the step.

teacher: Project the scale and ask the class to say the move before you press it. Use the left pan only button to show why one-sided changes break the equation. Misconception: students undo in the same order as the formula, so ask what was done to x first, then undo last-first.
